newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo banks make the first step to centralisation.
newsitem.headline: Yugo banks make the first step to centralisation.

text.p: Yugoslavia made the first step towards centralising its ailing banking system on Thursday by forming a new group of 20 banks with unified international credit and payment operations.

Beogradska Banka Group (BB-Group) gathers 20 member banks, including Beogradska banka AD, which signed an association agreement and operationally transferred some functions to Beogradska banka AD, Borka Vucic, head of the Beogradska Banka system, told an annual shareholders meeting.
Vucic insisted the idea was to rationalise an inefficient system employing around 12,000 people and to reduce costs.

"Today we need to make a decision on linking into Beogradska Banka Group, which based on its high rating at home and abroad would be able to secure fresh capital and support production growth," Vucic said.

The new giant association envisages an establishment of an independent bank rehabilitation agency to take over all debts from member banks and their clients but also to centralise their international payment and credit operations which will be performed through a single central account.

"Operating through one account does not mean an absolute centralisation of the entire business. On the contrary, payment operations, contacts and negotiations with our clients will be decentralised and banks will continue with the same operations and reap profits out of them," Vucic said.
She insisted one central account will only bring more control of external borrowing and reduce operating costs.
The bank rehabilitation agency will scan and identify all debts to be transferred to it and seek solutions for servicing the debt, its reduction or possible debt-for-equity swaps.

"This will be done by world standards... With an approach organised in this manner we go towards negotiations with the International Monetary Fund and the World bank, our London and Paris club creditors and simultaneously strengthen our position," Vucic added.
Vucic insisted BB-Group will not stand in the way to any government debt negotiations with foreign creditors, but will probably be the leader in debt talks with commercial creditors.
"Usually, one bank with most experience is chosen for a chief negotiator and Beogradska banka has the experience," she said.

Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic, addressing the meeting said: "I am sure that the strengthened system of Beogradska banka can successfully resolve reorganisation of our debts and secure fresh foreign capital."

Apart from securing fresh foreign credit support, the newly formed BB-Group will exert more effort to collect more than one billion dollars in Yugoslavia's external claims. The biggest debtors are former Soviet republics, Libya, Iraq and Syria.

The one billion dollars in foreign claims equals the amount of working capital needed for the local industries to kick-start production still running at an average 30 percent of installed capacities, Vucic said.

"With a reduced capital outflow, collected claims and fresh external capital, which we shall also secure through ownership transformation and privatisation, we can put an end to 15 years of net capital outflow and ensure growth," Vucic said.
BB-Group will set up its business council to create the statute of the group, regulating relations among member banks and joint banking functions.
The glamour of the ceremony was spoiled by two largest member banks -- Beobanka and Agrobanka -- whose directors walked out minutes before the signing began.

Beobanka, the largest Yugoslav commercial bank, was reluctunt to join the group until the statute specifies it can keep all its international payment and credit operations, and only in case of need co-finance important projects.

Beobanka is preparing its own bank rehabilitation model together with the CES-Mecon private research institute and the auditing and consulting company Price Waterhouse, to be presented to the public within ten days. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
